written: 2026-09-22, before any of the ownership ensembles below were run
question: The ring code writes its orders into distinct spatial Fourier modes of the bulk while it is held. What destroys that correspondence before the face is scored: the release of the clamp, the field feedback, or neither?
decomposition: Spatial Fourier (2D cosine, DCT-II) modes of the 11x11 grid, an orthonormal complete basis chosen without reference to the model's mechanics. Mode amplitudes are taken from the mean-subtracted pattern.
ownership: For an ensemble of codes sampled across the feasible region, each mode's amplitude is regressed on the coefficients. A mode is owned by an order when a quadratic regression on the coefficients explains at least half of its variance (R2 >= 0.5) and that order's first-order variance index holds at least half of the four orders' total. ownedVarianceShare is the share of the ensemble's pattern variance held by owned modes.
alreadySeen: At 256 codes, orders 0-3, field on: ownedVarianceShare 0.41 at the last held iteration (14 of 120 modes) and 0.00 at the trained moment 2173. P1 restates this at a larger ensemble and is confirmatory, not a fresh prediction.

conditions.baseline: orders 0-3, field feedback on, ring held 301 iterations then released, 1024 codes
conditions.heldThroughout: as baseline but the ring is held for all 3000 iterations, never released, 256 codes
conditions.fieldOff: as baseline but fieldEnabled = False, 1024 codes

predictions.name: P1 ownership during the hold, gone at the trained moment
predictions.criterion: baseline: ownedVarianceShare >= 0.3 at the last held iteration and < 0.1 at iteration 2173.

predictions.name: P2 the release is what destroys it
predictions.claim: Holding the ring forever preserves the correspondence.

predictions.name: P3 the field feedback scrambles the modes
predictions.claim: With the field's negative feedback off, the correspondence survives the release for longer.
predictions.criterion: fieldOff: ownedVarianceShare at iteration 2173 exceeds baseline's, and the iteration at which ownedVarianceShare first falls below 0.1 is later than baseline's.

predictions.name: P4 every order owns something
predictions.claim: Higher orders are not redundant: each writes into some mode of its own.
predictions.criterion: orders0to6: at the last held iteration, every order 0-6 is the top order of at least one owned mode.

predictions.name: P5 the face is not in the code's modes
predictions.claim: What the code can specify and what the face needs are different parts of the spectrum.
predictions.criterion: baseline: the owned modes at the last held iteration hold less than half of the face target's spectral energy.

interpretationIfP2Holds: The code's orders survive exactly as long as they are imposed; the pattern's own dynamics, once free, mixes them. The code would be a boundary condition the tissue reads and then overwrites, not a set of brushes.
interpretationIfP3Holds: The extracellular field's negative feedback, which is nonlocal and responds to gradients rather than levels, is the specific machinery that destroys the code's mode structure.
